answer: Sybil resistance here rests on per-identity bonding. Before an agent may act, it must lock a slashable stake and prove exclusive control of a hardware cipher key, so one operator scripting a gale of accounts needs a separate stake and device for each. The stake is priced above the expected payout of a single fake identity and is burned once collusion is proven, making every extra Sybil a net loss instead of free reach. Cheap pseudonyms become a relic: the attack can still be attempted, but its marginal cost now exceeds its marginal gain.
